newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to push for role on Middle East tour.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to push for role on Middle East tour.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, keen to win a bigger role for France in Middle East peacemaking, will visit four Arab states, Israel and the Palestinian territories on a tour from October 19 to 25, his office said on Friday.

The tour comes at a time when Arab leaders are looking to Europe to balance the perceived pro-Israeli bias of U.S. President Bill Clinton, campaigning for re-election, at a time of heightened tension in the region.

It will be Chirac's third and longest Middle East trip this year, underlining the importance the conservative Gaullist leader attaches to building French and European influence in a region long dominated by the United States.

His trip will begin with two days in Syria, which has refused to resume peace negotiations with Israel since it elected hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace.
France has built good relations with Damascus under Chirac after years of tension over Lebanon's sovereignty, human rights and incidents of Middle Eastern violence in Paris.
Syrian-backed Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik Hariri is a personal friend of Chirac and frequent visitor in Paris, where the billionaire politician has an elegant home.
Foreign Minister Herve de Charette helped broker a ceasefire between Israel and Lebanese Hizbollah guerrillas in April, partly due to contacts with Syria and its ally, Iran.

Chirac will then travel to Israel and the Palestinian territories on October 21-23 to try to nudge forward difficult negotiations on expanding Palestinian self-rule and eventually granting the Palestinians full self-determination.

Before he goes there, the French foreign ministry said on Friday it was sending senior official Bertrand Dufourcq on a fact-finding mission to Eygpt, Israel and the Palestinian territories to prepare the visit and "facilitate the success of ongoing talks".

The French leader has played host to both Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the last month. Arafat appealed to the EU to play a role in negotiations with the Jewish state, while the Israelis have been determined to stick to U.S. mediation, which they consider more favourable to them.

Chirac will visit Jordan on October 23-24 and then make short stops in Lebanon and Egypt, both of which he visited earlier this year, to round off his trip, stressing his attachment to keeping pro-peace Arab leaders informed.
